Cutaneous Leukocytoclastic Vasculitis: Skin biopsy from the ankle revealed a perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with prominent neutrophils and associated fibrinoid necrosis of vessels consistent with 'leukocytoclastic' vasculitis
Rash on the elbows, ankles, and feet, starting as red macules and progressing to vesico-pustular lesions followed by crusting
Pustules and crusts around the elbows, ankles, and feet, sparing the buttocks
Clinical signs of synovitis in the wrists, proximal interphalangeal, and metacarpophalangeal joints, as well as both ankles
perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and fibrinoid necrosis of vessels
Leukocytoclastic Vasculitis: skin lesions with purpura or ulcers
Erythema Nodosum: tender skin nodules on lower extremities
Polyarteritis Nodosa: systemic symptoms like fever and weight loss
Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis: upper and lower respiratory tract symptoms
